messages.content: "John has $5000 that he wants to invest. He is considering two options. The first option is a savings account that compounds interest quarterly at an annual rate of 4% for 5 years. The second option is a bond that offers simple interest at an annual rate of 3.5% for 5 years. How much would John have at the end of 5 years for both options?"

message.content:
**Savings‑account (compound quarterly)**  

| Symbol | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Principal \(P\) | \$5 000 |
| Annual nominal rate \(\text{APR}\) | 4 % → \(r = 0.04\) |
| Compounds per year \(n\) | 4 |
| Time \(t\) | 5 years |

Future value for compound interest  
\(A_{\text{comp}} = P\,\bigl(1+\frac{r}{n}\bigr)^{nt}\)

\[
\begin{aligned}
A_{\text{comp}}
&= 5\,000\;\Bigl(1+\frac{0.04}{4}\Bigr)^{4\times5}\\[4pt]
&= 5\,000\;(1+0.01)^{20}\\[4pt]
&= 5\,000\;(1.01)^{20}\\[4pt]
&\approx 5\,000\;\times 1.220206\\[4pt]
&\approx \$6\,101.03 .
\end{aligned}
\]

---

**Bond (simple interest)**  

| Symbol | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Principal \(P\) | \$5 000 |
| Annual rate \(r\) | 3.5 % → \(0.035\) |
| Time \(t\) | 5 years |

Simple‑interest total  
\(A_{\text{simp}} = P\,(1 + rt)\)

\[
\begin{aligned}
A_{\text{simp}}
&= 5\,000\,[1 + (0.035)(5)] \\[4pt]
&= 5\,000\,[1 + 0.175] \\[4pt]
&= 5\,000 \times 1.175 \\[4pt]
&= \$5\,875 .
\end{aligned}
\]

---

### Result Summary

| Option | Final Amount After 5 Years |
|--------|---------------------------|
| Quarterly‑compounded savings account | **\$6 101.03** |
| Simple‑interest bond | **\$5 875** |

The savings account earns approximately **$226 higher** than the bond over five years because of the power of compounding each quarter.
